summary: Tender cow foot in a thick, spicy palm oil and utazi sauce thickened with potash, served warm with sliced onions.
story: Nkwobi is an Igbo delicacy of cow foot cooked until soft and coated in a thick, spiced palm-oil sauce. It is commonly served at bars, restaurants and gatherings, often with a cold drink.

steps.title: Boil the cow foot
steps.text: Place the cow foot in a pot with the quartered onion, cubes and salt. Cover with water and pressure-cook for 45 minutes or simmer 2 to 2 1/2 hours. It is ready when the skin is very soft and gelatinous and the meat pulls from the bone.

steps.title: Drain and keep warm
steps.text: Lift out the cow foot and keep it hot. Save a small cup of the stock in case you need to loosen the sauce.

steps.title: Make the potash liquid
steps.text: Stir the potash into the water, let the grit settle, and pour off only the clear liquid. A little of this makes the palm oil thicken.

steps.title: Whip the palm oil
steps.text: Add the palm oil to about 1 tbsp of the clear potash liquid in a pot and stir over very low heat until it turns thick, creamy and pale orange-yellow. This is the characteristic nkwobi texture.

steps.title: Add the spices
steps.text: Stir in the ehuru, crayfish, scotch bonnet and seasoning cube. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes just until warm and fragrant. Add a spoonful of reserved stock if it is too thick.

steps.title: Coat the meat
steps.text: Fold the hot cow foot into the sauce until each piece is thoroughly coated. Taste and add salt if needed.

steps.title: Finish with utazi
steps.text: Stir in most of the utazi and half of the sliced onion. Serve warm in a bowl or on a wooden plate, topped with the remaining onion and utazi.

tips: Add the potash liquid gradually. Too much leaves a harsh, soapy taste.
Do not boil the sauce hard once the palm oil is whipped or it will split and turn oily.
Utazi is bitter by design, so use it in moderation.
Serve warm; the sauce stiffens as it cools.

swaps.swap: A tiny pinch of baking soda dissolved in water thickens the palm oil in a similar way, though less authentically.
Use a few leaves of endive or rocket for similar bitterness, or leave out and add extra onion.
Substitute a small pinch of ground nutmeg plus black pepper.

name: Nkwobi
